content: Do not pour this medication down a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. Important Usage Information: This document is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Medroxyprogesterone is a type of hormone known as a progestin. It mimics the natural progesterone produced by your body and is prescribed to replace this hormone when your body does not produce enough. This medication has multiple uses, including being part of combination hormone replacement therapy with estrogens to alleviate menopause symptoms such as hot flashes. How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, following the prescribed dosing schedule carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor. For treating stopped menstrual periods (amenorrhea) or abnormal uterine bleeding, this medication is typically taken once daily for 5 to 10 days during the second half of the planned menstrual cycle or as directed by your doctor. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, changes in vaginal discharge, mood swings, blurred vision, dizziness, drowsiness, or weight changes. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this medication, especially when used with estrogen products, may rarely cause serious and potentially fatal blood clot-related problems, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs, legs, or eyes. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice. Precautions: Before taking medroxyprogesterone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. Some Canadian brands of this product may contain inactive ingredients (such as soybean), which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Individuals allergic to peanuts may also be allergic to soy. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin (melasma), which can worsen with sunlight. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of medroxyprogesterone from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include rifamycins (such as rifampin). This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular Monitoring: Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-examinations and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
